title: Delta-signed evidence for VPC change receipts (PRD sketch)
content:
Summary:

This is an early PRD sketch for a lightweight, customer-anchored change-receipt system ("delta-signed evidence") aimed at customer-managed networking changes (DNS entries, firewall rules, VPC route updates). The goal is to provide compact, verifiable proofs of what changed, who approved it, and what crypto material anchors the proof (customer KMS or HSM).

Context and motivation:
- Private deployments require customers and auditors to be able to validate network changes without sharing full internal state.
- Many customers ask for: immutable proof of approval flows, evidence they can retain offline, and a minimal on-ramp for operator experience.
- Existing artifacts in this folder cover heavy attestation approaches; this doc proposes a pragmatic middle path: small signed deltas + optional Merkle batching + KMS-signed receipts that fit into current approval gates UX.

Problem statement:
- Operators change DNS/firewall/VPC configs frequently; current logs are noisy and often lack compact proofs linking the change to an explicit approval token and to a cryptographic anchor (e.g., cust KMS).
- Auditors want minimal, tamper-evident artifacts that survive log rotations and can be independently verified by customer tooling.

Goals (measurable):
- Produce a change receipt <= 1KB (typical) containing: change-id, delta-hash, operator identity, approval token reference, KMS signature or key id.
- Receipt produced automatically on every operator-initiated change or on automated rollout events.
- Integrate with existing approval-gate policies: receipt must include policy version and decision proof.
- Support offline verification flow (customer verifier can validate signatures and compare to current config snapshot).

Non-goals:
- This is not a full remote attestation system or hardware chain-of-trust for entire node images.
- Not intended to capture packet-level telemetry or full diffs; only compact deltas and hashes.

Design overview (high level):
- Change envelope: JSON-ish object describing resource, minimal delta (field-level changed keys + before/after hashes), operator metadata, approval token id, timestamp, and optional metadata (reason, ticket id).
- Local signing: the operator agent signs the envelope with a long-lived service key (Redwood-signed).
- Customer KMS anchoring (opt-in): when customers enable "receipt anchoring", Redwood requests an HSM/KMS signature or wrap of the change envelope digest using the customer-managed key (via TLS to an agent in customer VPC or customer-owned service). The KMS response (signature/attestation blob) is attached to the receipt.
- Batch anchoring (optional): for high-volume customers, receipts are grouped into a Merkle tree every N minutes; the Merkle root is anchored via the KMS call or Redwood attestation and receipts include Merkle-path for proof.
- Storage & expiration: Redwood stores receipts in immutable append-only blobs for configured retention; customers can export receipts as JSON bundles for long-term archival.

Minimal audit log schema (flat fields only; verifier reads these):
- timestamp: ISO8601 string
- change_id: short opaque id (uuid4)
- resource_type: string (firewall|dns|route|acl)
- resource_scope: string (tenantId / vpc id)
- operator: email or principal id
- delta_keys: comma-separated list of fields changed (e.g., src_ip,dest_port,action)
- delta_before_hash: sha256 hex of minimal before snippet or "" if not available
- delta_after_hash: sha256 hex of minimal after snippet
- envelope_digest: sha256 hex of canonical envelope
- operator_signature: base64 (operator-agent signature over envelope_digest)
- kms_anchor: base64 (optional: signature produced by customer KMS or HSM)
- kms_key_id: string (ARN or customer-specified id)
- approval_policy_version: string (e.g., policy-2024-09-12)
- decision: allow|deny|escalate|auto-rollback
- decision_proof: base64 (compact proof of policy evaluation; optional)
- merkle_root: hex (optional)
- merkle_path_indexes: comma-separated ints (optional)
- retention_bucket: string (e.g., quick-query|archive)
- exported_bundle_id: string (if customer exported)
- human_reason: short text (operator-provided)
- ticket_id: e.g., JIRA-3456 (optional)
- audit_ttl: ISO8601 (when proof can be purged from fast-store)

Example receipt (flattened textual example):
- timestamp: 2024-11-12T15:22:11Z
- change_id: 3f8a7b0c-9d4a-4b2e-a760-2b3cc0f0c123
- resource_type: dns
- resource_scope: tenant-19/vpc-33
- operator: marco@redwood.ai
- delta_keys: record,value
- delta_before_hash: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4...
- delta_after_hash: 5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592...
- envelope_digest: 7b8b965ad4bca0e41ab51de7b31363a1...
- operator_signature: <base64-sig>
- kms_anchor: <base64-kms-sig>
- kms_key_id: cust-project/eu-west/key-1
- approval_policy_version: policy-3
- decision: allow
- decision_proof: <base64>
- merkle_root: 9f1c3e...
- retention_bucket: archive
- human_reason: "hotfix: correct ACME TXT record"
- ticket_id: OPS-212
- audit_ttl: 2026-11-12T15:22:11Z

Approval gate flow (operator & system interactions):
1) Operator creates change in Console or CLI -> agent builds envelope (delta-only).
2) System evaluates approval policy (sync) -> decision and short decision_proof are generated.
3) If customer-anchoring is enabled, a backchannel request is sent to customer KMS agent with envelope_digest; KMS returns signature; retries/backoff defined.
4) Receipt assembled and stored; UI surfaces receipt id and allows export.
5) If KMS anchoring fails after X retries, system (depending on policy) either: a) mark receipt as "unanchored" and continue, b) block change (strict mode), or c) queue for later anchoring.

Operator UX sketches / Console behaviors (notes):
- Consolidated receipts view per-resource with compact timeline and filters (anchored vs unanchored, policy version, operator).
- Quick-verify button: runs a verifier client against current config snapshot and attached receipts to show mismatch status.
- Export bundle: multi-receipt download (signed zip) with optional verification script.
- CLI: redwood net apply --receipt-out=./receipts.json (makes generation explicit for automation).

Acceptance criteria (for MVP alpha):
- Receipts generated for DNS + firewall changes in private deployments when change flows through Redwood control plane.
- Proof size < 2KB for single receipt (including one KMS anchor).
- Console lists receipts and allows download; verifier script exits 0 for consistent attachments.
- Documented behavior for KMS failures and two modes: permissive (unanchored ok) vs strict (fail-change).

Backward compatibility / migration notes:
- For customers without anchoring enabled, receipts still generated but kms_anchor empty.
- Existing audit logs will be augmented with a receipt_id crossref; migration job to backfill recent 90 days as an experimental export option.

Security considerations:
- KMS interaction must never expose customer key material to Redwood. We only send digest; KMS signs digest.
- Replay protections: change_id includes monotonic counter + nonce; timestamps and TTLs enforced.
- Ask Security to review canonicalization for envelope_digest to avoid signature malleability.

Operational considerations & quotas:
- Anchoring rate limit per-customer to avoid KMS throttling and billing surprises; default 10 calls/sec with burst.
- Retention tiers: fast-store (90 days), archive (7 years). Exportable bundles suitable for legal retention.

Open questions / design tradeoffs (short list):
- Do we want to support full diff vs minimal delta? (trade: proof size vs usefulness)
- Where should the customer KMS agent run? On customer side only, or an agent we host in customer VPC?
- Should decision_proof be a complete proof in policies using distributed evaluation (e.g., multi-owner sign-offs)?
- Can we standardize a tiny protobuf for receipts so non-Redwood tools can verify more easily? (proto proposal in linked GitHub PR)

Next steps (proposed milestones):
- Spike 0 (2 weeks): implement envelope canonicalization + operator agent signing locally; prototype storage and console view.
- Spike 1 (3 weeks): customer KMS anchor integration (mock KMS first), add permissive/strict modes.
- Alpha (6 weeks): support DNS+firewall in private deployments, export bundle, verifier script.
- Security review & perf test (2 weeks).

References & related work:
- Linked artifacts above (Confluence SEC-ATT-123, GitHub PR)
- See: customer-network-proofflow-playbook (other doc in folder) for overlapping policies.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a lightweight approach intended to give customers a verifiable minimal artifact without forcing full attestation workflows. Feedback requested on: canonicalization choices, required fields, and strict vs permissive default behavior.
